subject: FastReach: sudden spike in streaming chat p99 during evening peak
messages:
From: Alyssa Trent <alyssa.trent@fastreach.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-07T19:05:12-07:00
Subject: Realtime chat errors + huge p99 spike (7:00pm PST)

Hi Grace,

We're seeing a large uptick in p99 latency and an increase in 502/504 errors on the hosted streaming chat endpoint starting at ~18:58 PT. Traffic is our usual evening peak (concurrency ~3.6k). Users report long stalls and socket disconnects; some sessions are getting repeated reconnection attempts.

Quick details:
- p95 ~ 450ms (ok) but p99 jumped to ~5.2s and many 504s on the SSE endpoint
- Error samples attached (sse-error-sample.log)
- This is affecting our paid customers on the growth tier; they're already on chat and complaining to CS.

Can you confirm if this is on Redwood's side or something in our integration? We need a status and ETA — our CS team is holding until we have clarity.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Trent
Head of Platform, FastReach AI
alyssa.trent@fastreach.ai

---
Attachment: sse-error-sample.log (text)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Trent <alyssa.trent@fastreach.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-07T19:11:03-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat errors + huge p99 spike (7:00pm PST)

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. Sorry you're hitting this during peak.

We're looking now. Looping Dev (SRE/runtime) and Markus (infra) — can you confirm whether the clients were using long-poll SSE or websocket fallback for these sessions? Also want to confirm whether you're on the hosted plan (yes, you are) so we can prioritize capacity.

Action items for us:
- Dev: grab request traces and identify any tail queuing or KV cache misses; check autoscaler logs.
- Markus: validate GPU pool saturation and gateway LB health; consider quick scale bump.

I'll keep you updated within 20 minutes.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Alyssa Trent <alyssa.trent@fastreach.ai>
Date: 2027-09-07T19:25:47-07:00
Subject: RE: Realtime chat errors + huge p99 spike (7:00pm PST)

Thanks — I pulled the first 200 request traces from the timeframe and attached a filtered sample in the zip. Preliminary notes:
- We observe a small but concentrated set of connection accept queues on the front-line gateway for instances serving SSE; a buildup of long-running requests with large initial prefix lengths seems to be causing KV cache thrashing.
- Autoscaler did not trigger additional workers fast enough for the percentile tail; scale policy currently has a cooldown that held it back.
- There's a recent kernel-level optimization we rolled last week that changed the async IO backoff which may be interacting poorly with very bursty long-lived SSE connections.

Immediate mitigations applied (19:22 PT):
- Bypassed the cooldown and forced +30% capacity on the affected pool.
- Temporarily lowered per-connection max_pending_tokens to reduce head-of-line blocking for new accepts.
- Enabled a conservative prefix cache bypass to reduce cache churn.

Attachments: sre_diagnostics_20270907.zip (traces + perf counters)

I'll continue to watch graphs; initial telemetry shows p99 falling from ~5.2s to ~2.1s but still above baseline.

—Dev
Dev Patel
SRE/Runtime Engineer
dev.patel@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Alyssa Trent <alyssa.trent@fastreach.ai>
Date: 2027-09-07T19:40:12-07:00
Subject: RE: Realtime chat errors + huge p99 spike (7:00pm PST)

Update from infra side: we increased pool size and adjusted the gateway connection limit at 19:30 PT. Key points:
- Scaled affected GPU pool by +2 nodes (warmup applied) and drained a misbehaving host.
- Increased LB worker count and raised max concurrent accepts per worker by 20%.
- Flushed a stale rate-limiter bucket that had anomalous token decay behavior.

Telemetry after actions: p99 down to ~1.1s; 504s down by ~80%. Some customers may still see degraded tails while caches warm.

We'll keep an eye on it and coordinate a roll-back of the temporary knob changes once steady.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure
markus.klein@redwood.com
From: Alyssa Trent <alyssa.trent@fastreach.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-07T20:05:54-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat errors + huge p99 spike (7:00pm PST)

Thanks Grace / team — we see clear improvement after your changes; p99 is ~1.0–1.3s now and errors are much reduced. Still a small subset of sessions show reconnection loops (maybe the ones that hit the earlier 5s stalls).

Two asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood provide a short mitigation report and the expected RCA timeline? Our legal/ops folks are asking for impact details.
2) Given the customer impact during the evening commercial peak, would Redwood consider a one-time credit for the affected usage window? We can share client IDs if helpful.

Appreciate the fast response — Lauren from our account team is now on the thread for billing.

—Alyssa
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Trent <alyssa.trent@fastreach.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-07T21:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat errors + huge p99 spike (7:00pm PST) — summary & next steps

Alyssa — thanks for the confirmation and for escalating billing to Lauren. Quick summary and next steps: 

What happened (short):
- During your evening peak we saw concentrated request-accept queuing on SSE workers combined with KV cache churn; autoscaler cooldown delayed capacity reaction and a recent async IO backoff change amplified tail latency for long-lived connections.

Immediate resolution:
- Forced +30% capacity, removed the cooldown, increased LB workers, and applied a temporary cache-bypass and connection accept tuning. Result: p99 reduced from ~5.2s -> ~1.1s; 504s dropped ~80%.

Next actions / RCA plan:
- Postmortem investigation (owner: Dev) to validate the async IO backoff interaction and update scale policies to avoid cooldown blocking for long-lived streaming workloads.
- Temp changes will be rolled back carefully after metric stabilization; will coordinate a canary first.
- We'll produce a short mitigation report and full RCA within 72 hours.

Credits / commercial:
- Lauren, can you please propose a one-time credit for the affected window? My recommendation is a usage credit equivalent to the evening peak surcharge; happy to support that ask with the mitigation timeline.

Meeting:
- Proposed postmortem sync: 2027-09-09 10:00 PT (30m). I'll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: fastreach-mitigation-summary.pdf (executive summary of actions taken)

Again — sorry for the disruption. We'll follow up with the RCA and the Stats dashboard link once it's compiled.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
